_comment: Tier-2 for skfem adaptive_poisson#3, verified 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1. Claim: m.f2t is (2, n_facets) with -1 in the second row for boundary facets, and dereferencing f2t[1, fi] as an element id without the >= 0 check raises IndexError 'index -1 is out of bounds'. Ran: MeshTri().refined(2) -- 32 elements, 56 facets -- inspecting f2t, indexing m.t by f2t[1] under catch_warnings, and comparing against the guarded interior selection. Printed: the shape and the -1 sentinel are exact, and the 16 entries equal to -1 are precisely m.boundary_facets(). THE QUOTED IndexError NEVER FIRES: numpy reads -1 as 'the last element', so m.t[:, m.f2t[1]] returns a full (3, 56) array with the LAST element's connectivity silently substituted on all 16 boundary facets -- no exception, no warning, and the SAME SHAPE a correct result would have, so neither try/except nor a shape check catches it. All 16 substituted columns differ from the real neighbouring element, so a jump computed that way picks up an unrelated element from the far side of the mesh. The guard that works is the mask f2t[1] >= 0, which selects exactly the 40 interior facets. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 applies the documented guard at the dereference site -- the facet list fed to m.t[:, f2t[1]] becomes the masked interior set np.nonzero(f2t[1] >= 0)[0] instead of every facet, so no -1 is dereferenced. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on skfem 12.0.1: the unmutated run matches all 12 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 removes 'neighbour_array_has_the_expected_shape=True' (the array is (3, 40), not (3, 56)), 'boundary_columns_equal_the_last_element=True' and 'every_boundary_facet_is_corrupted=True' (no boundary facet is dereferenced any more) and fires the forbidden 'FAIL:', so the fixture goes red. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py FIXED 2026-08-08: dropped neighbour_array_has_the_expected_shape. Inside the no-exception branch where it was printed, m.t[:, f2t[1][fsel]] with fsel = np.arange(nf) has shape (3, nf) by construction, so the line could not be False and only restated indexing_by_minus_one_raises=False, which is asserted separately. The shape is still printed, just not asserted as a finding. The two siblings the screen also flagged, boundary_columns_equal_the_last_element and every_boundary_facet_is_corrupted, are KEPT: both compare the wrapped columns against real m.t columns and would go False if skfem's sentinel were not -1 or if the last element owned a boundary facet.
